gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Trio 3 Pro's screens can't reach full brightness on laptop power alone (Macworld) or that Notebookcheck measured a single-cable USB-C monitor falling from 206 nits on its adapter to 88 nits; none says that full brightness on one cable needs a wall adapter in the extender's own USB-C port.
standout_why: Compared against itechguides.com 'Best Laptop Screen Extenders in 2025' (cited in chat 1). That page says it did no hands-on testing. It lists the Trio 3 Pro's 65 W pass-through as a spec and says 'the displays themselves consume power', but gives no figure and no reviewer measurement. ChatGPT's two answers call single-cable setups 'convenient' but never mention that brightness drops on laptop power. I couldn't read the other cited rival, mobilepixels.us/products/trio, because it returned HTTP 429 twice; the maker's page wouldn't carry an independent measurement anyway. The search-result titles of the other top results (deskgearhq, theofficejournal, nucleusky, techpp, gradedpicks) don't point to lab work, but I didn't open them.
decides: This confirms the Trio 3 Pro, rather than a FOPO dual, as the two-added-screen choice for a one-port laptop. It also adds a condition the page must state. Notebookcheck found that FOPO's extender needs one cable per screen, so it doesn't fit a single port. The Trio can run both screens from one cable with Mobile Pixels' driver. At full brightness, though, it needs a wall adapter in its own USB-C port, and that adapter also passes up to 65 W back to the laptop (Macworld). For a one-port laptop that is a plus: the laptop charges through the same single cable. It also means the full-brightness, one-cable setup isn't fully portable away from a wall socket. The single-screen Duex Max DS pick is unchanged. I found no independent measurement for it.

findings.label: Brightness on laptop power alone (named reviewer)
findings.value: Below the rated 300-nit maximum; full brightness needs a power adapter in one of the Trio's USB-C ports
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review (Macworld, Simon Jary, Apr 2, 2026)
findings.note: Simon Jary, tested on a 14-inch MacBook Pro, quoted: 'the Trio's screens can't draw enough power from the connected laptop to allow for maximum screen brightness'; 'you need to attach a power adapter to one of the Trio's USB-C ports'; 'That will also passthrough up to 65W of power to your laptop.' This is a reviewer's finding with no measured nits figure.

findings.label: Cables and driver as reviewed
findings.value: Two included USB-C cables; both screens on one cable with Mobile Pixels' free software; no driver if the laptop has two DP-capable USB-C ports
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review (Macworld, Simon Jary, Apr 2, 2026)
findings.note: Macworld also says base M1 and M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo drive only one external monitor natively and need the software. Weight as reviewed: 4.13 lb (1.9 kg). Macworld quoted $499.99 on Apr 2, 2026; that is not today's price.

findings.label: Brightness on computer-only power (second named reviewer)
findings.value: Maximum brightness limited when powered only from the computer (no figure given)
findings.source_title: Test Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro (CHIP.pl, Kacper Cembrowski, 18.09.2026)
findings.note: Quote: 'przy zasilaniu wyłącznie z komputera ich maksymalna jasność jest ograniczona' (when powered only by the computer, their maximum brightness is limited). findings.label: Brightness without external power (named reviewer)
findings.value: Maximum brightness limited unless the Mobile Pixels power supply is connected first (no figure given)

findings.product: FOPO 12-inch triple monitor extender (an older FOPO model, not the S1 or S7)
findings.label: Measured brightness, contrast, gamut, accuracy (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: 193.1 cd/m² max, 177.4 cd/m² average; 247:1 contrast (0.75 cd/m² black); 79% sRGB; ColorChecker ΔE 4.59 (0.84 calibrated); greyscale ΔE 6.8
findings.source_title: FOPO 12-inch triple monitor extender review (Notebookcheck, Allen Ngo, Jul 23, 2022)
findings.note: This is the only lab measurement of a FOPO extender I found, and it is a different, older model from the FOPO screens we link. Use it only as an indication of the brand's panels. Connection finding: 'each of the two displays require their own cables for power and video'; with two USB-C DP ports, one USB-C cable per screen; without them, HDMI plus a separate power cable. On an HP Pavilion Plus 14, the laptop recharged through a USB-C AC adapter plugged into one FOPO monitor.

findings.label: Measured brightness on adapter vs single USB-C cable, and power draw (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: 206 nits max on its AC adapter vs 88 nits on a single cable for video and power; 12.2 W at minimum and 14.5 W at maximum brightness
findings.source_title: AirTab 15.6-inch Portable Touchscreen Monitor Review: Sleek But Too Dim (Notebookcheck, Allen Ngo, Jun 12, 2020)
findings.note: This is not a candidate. It's the only named lab figure I found that puts numbers on the single-cable brightness drop, so it works as a general illustration. The drop is 206 − 88 = 118 nits, or 88/206 ≈ 43% of adapter brightness. Notebookcheck also reports 10–16 W while idling on the desktop.
